items.title: The law of Arratia's random integer J_x^*: P[J_x^* = j] = (1/(j log x))(1 + O(1/log x))
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.difficulty_reason: The claim pins down the exact law of Arratia's random integer J_x^* = prod_{i=1}^K Q_i^*, built from the transformed Poisson process R^*, up to relative error O(1/log x). The proof does not estimate P[J_x^* = j] by inclusion-exclusion: it first identifies the law of the partial product I_t^* from the Dirichlet series prod_q exp((Lambda(q)/(q^{1+t} log q))(q^{-s} - 1)) = zeta(1+t+s)/zeta(1+t), which forces P[I_t^* = i] = i^{-1-t}/zeta(1+t) (source 774-778), and then writes the indicator of {J_x^* = j} as a sum over Poisson points with Q^* > x/j and evaluates it with the Mecke equation (778-787). The remaining step is a genuine asymptotic in t: Mertens plus partial summation give sum_{q>x/j} Lambda(q)/q^{1+t} = (x/j)^{-t}(1+O(t))/t, and the split at t = 1 using 1/zeta(1+t) = t + O(t^2) produces the main term 1/(j log x) (788-800).

primary.label: Lemma lem:probaj (Arratia): law of the random integer J_x^* built from the transformed Poisson process

proof_spans.label: complete author proof: Poisson prime-power counts, Dirichlet-series inversion, Mecke expansion, Mertens partial summation and the zeta expansion at t = 0
